theorem rhom_supported_quasiCoherent_support_part
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (K L : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hzero : ∀ n : ℤ,
      IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj L))) :
    ∀ n : ℤ,
      IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj
            ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
              X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op K, L))))

title: Support preservation for derived internal Hom
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], K and L objects of its derived category of module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category], and T a closed subset. If every cohomology sheaf of L restricts to zero on the open complement of T, then every cohomology sheaf of RSheafHom(K,L) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] restricts to zero there. No quasi-coherence, boundedness, pseudo-coherence or perfectness assumption is required.

proof.text: Let U be the open complement of T. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology, so the hypothesis makes every cohomology object of L restricted to U zero. Cohomology detects zero in the derived category, hence L restricted to U is a zero object. Derived internal Hom commutes with restriction to U. Internal Hom into a zero object is zero: represent the first argument by any complex and the second by the zero K-injective complex; every term of its Hom complex is a product of zero module sheaves. Consequently every cohomology sheaf of RHom(K,L) restricts to zero on U. This argument also covers U empty, T empty, and T equal to X; it requires no pseudo-coherence or perfectness assumption.
